answer: In an agent marketplace trading marble, sable, and compute, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting one deposit across a thousand identities creates no extra influence, so a ripple of new accounts cannot amplify a vote. To gain 30% of voting power, an attacker must acquire and lock 30% of all staked tokens, tying up capital and bearing its price risk.
